# What is a statistical test, and when to use it?

## What is a median? A mean?

The mean is the arithmetic average of a dataset. The median is the middle value when the data is sorted in order (Source: Google Gemini, see References)

## What is a variance? A standard deviation?

Variance is the average squard deviation of each data point frome the mean.

The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which expresses the dispersion of the values. (Source: Jamet, Introduction aux statistiques, Licence STAPS Marseille)

## What is a normal distribution?

A normal distribution is a is a continuous and symmetric. There is the same % in the 2 sides of the mean. And the mean= the median = mode. It is a bell-shaped probability distribution where data clusters around the mean, with 68% of values within one standard deviation and 95% within two. (Source: Jamet, Introduction aux statistiques, Licence STAPS Marseille)

## What is a statistical test?

A statistical test uses sample data to test a hypothesis and draw conclusions about a larger population. (Source: Google Gemini, see References)

## When to use a statistical test?

We use a statistical test to check if the results in your data are real, or if they just happened by chance. (Source: Google Gemini, see References)

## What is a parametric test? A non-parametric test?

A parametric test assumes that your data follows a specific pattern (usually a normal distribution), while a non-parametric test doesn't make any assumptions about how the data is distributed. (Source: Jamet, Introduction aux statistiques, Licence STAPS Marseille)

## What are the assumptions of parametric tests?

Common assumptions include normal distribution, equal variances between groups, independent observations, and data measured on an interval or ratio scale. (Source: Jamet, Introduction aux statistiques, Licence STAPS Marseille)

## What are the assumptions of non-parametric tests?

Non-parametric tests assume that observations are independent, data is at least ordinal, and for tests like Mann-Whitney U, that both groups have a similar distribution shape. (Source: Google Gemini, see References) 

## What is a p-value? 
A p-value is the probability of obtaining test results at least as extreme as the observed results, assuming the null hypothesis is true. (Source: Jamet, Introduction aux statistiques, Licence STAPS Marseille)

## What is the risk of error when using a statistical test?

The primary risks are a Type I error alpha, which is rejecting a true null hypothesis (false positive), and a Type II error beta, which is failing to reject a false null hypothesis (false negative). (Source: Jamet, Introduction aux statistiques, Licence STAPS Marseille)

## What is the difference between a paired and an unpaired test?

A paired test compares two set of measurements from the same group (like before and after a treatment), while an unpaired test compares two completely independent groups. (Source: Jamet, Introduction aux statistiques, Licence STAPS Marseille)
